what: Figures on a shipped or served surface that no rule reads and that do not carry their conditions in their own sentence, and why each one is allowed to stand. Read by scripts/policy-sentences.py.
how: The walk is deny by default. Every quantity on every surface has to be read by a rule, refused for being said of every stamp, carrying its conditions in its own sentence, or named here. An entry covers the figures it lists, on the surfaces it lists, in the sentence it quotes, and nothing else on any of the three: reword the sentence and the excuse stops covering it, which is the point of quoting it in full. An entry with no reason is refused outright, and so is one naming a reason this file does not write out. An entry that matched nothing on a run that read every surface it names is refused too, so the list cannot quietly fill up with excuses for sentences that have gone.
state: Forty entries on 2026-09-16, the day the walk went in, over 1620 sentences and 476 figures, of which 51 are read by a rule and 347 carry their conditions in their own sentence. Forty is the size of what was never being read rather than a queue of work: the rules and the copy already answer seven figures in eight, and the entries below are the classes neither reaches. A new figure on a surface is rare, so this list is expected to stay about this length. The twenty-one entries reading "the conditions are in the table line this figure sits in" or "a field of the committed receipt" are the ones to look at first when the content reader learns to hand a table line over in one piece.

reasons.a worked example of the algorithm: The numbers are a hypothetical, invented to show what Marzullo's algorithm does with a server that agrees with everything. No machine was measured and nothing here is offered as a reading, so there are no conditions to state and there is no artefact to hold it to. The arithmetic is checkable from the sentence itself, which is what a worked example is for.
reasons.arithmetic on two readings stated above: The figure is the difference between, or the range across, readings whose date, machine, cadence and round count are given in the sentences above it in the same paragraph. The conditions are on the page and they are one sentence up. Quoting them again inside this sentence would make the comparison unreadable, which is the thing the paragraph exists to do.
reasons.a target rather than a reading: The figure is where the product is being built towards and not what anything reached. It has no conditions because nothing was measured, and rule 9 of what this product may say allows prose to be forward-looking. It is said in words that make it a target and never as a width anybody can reproduce.
reasons.a setting read off the shipped policy: The figure is a constant this code ships, stated in prose beside the behaviour it causes. It is not a measurement, so it has no conditions; what holds it honest is the code, and the sentences around it name the constant.
reasons.a threshold of the method rather than a: The figure is the point below which the method cannot see anything, which follows from what is being compared rather than from any reading. Nothing was measured to arrive at it and there is nothing for a reader to reproduce.
reasons.the span the readings covered: The figure names how long the readings ran for or which day they were taken on, inside a sentence whose subject is the share of readings refused. It is the scope of a measurement rather than a measurement, and the readings themselves are stated with their conditions in the sentences above.
reasons.a bound of the verifier, held to its own: The figure is one of the sanity bounds the free verifier applies, given in the table in docs/verifier.md with the reason for each beside it. It is a limit this code chose rather than anything measured, and the table is the record of the choice.
reasons.a field of the committed receipt, render: The figure is one number out of the receipt committed at crates/verify/tests/data/a-real-stamp/receipt.cbor, printed on the page as the receipt states it, with no sentence around it to carry conditions. Its conditions are the receipt itself and the paragraphs beside it on the page. tests/check-messaging-figures.py at the product root holds this figure to that file and scripts/three-surfaces.sh holds the page to the tree, so changing the number breaks both of those as well as this entry, which quotes it in full.
reasons.the wording of a message the product sho: The figure is inside a line the running product prints to whoever is using it, quoted on the page as an example of what they will see. It states what the product does next rather than anything measured about a clock, so there are no conditions to give.
reasons.a fact about the page rather than about: The figure describes the page a reader is looking at, how long an animation runs or how often it repeats, and says nothing about a clock, a bound or a receipt. There is no measurement behind it and nothing for a reader to reproduce beyond watching the page.
reasons.the conditions are in the table line thi: The page puts the figure in a value field and the conditions in the note beside it, which is one line of a table a reader sees whole and this check reads as two strings. The content reader yields each string on its own, so the conditions are on the page and one field away rather than absent. That is a shortcoming of the reader rather than of the copy, and these entries go the moment the reader hands a table line over in one piece.
